sources.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture Notes for 18.155: Distributions, Elliptic Regularity, and Applications to PDEs (current 2026 revision)
sources.locator: Exercise 11.3, printed p. 135; Section 12.1.1, Proposition 12.1 and Remark 12.2, printed pp. 139-140; Section 12.1.2, Definition 12.3 and properties (1)-(5), printed pp. 140-141

contents.name: Exercise 11.3: smooth polynomially bounded derivatives multiply Schwartz space and tempered distributions
contents.support: The published general multiplier lemma is used only after the local bracket derivative estimates are proved.

contents.name: Proposition 12.1: integer-order weak derivatives and weighted Fourier data are equivalent
contents.reason: FR-6 owns comparison with derivative-sum W^{k,2} norms under the repository's 2pi transform; the present pair constructs the real-order completion.

contents.name: Remark 12.2: the Sobolev Fourier condition controls local L2 and high-frequency decay
contents.support: The positive Japanese-bracket weight fixes low frequencies and defines the inhomogeneous candidate norm.

contents.name: Definition 12.3: real-order Sobolev space as weighted Fourier distributions
contents.support: The source definition is proved equivalent to this pair's prior completion definition.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (1): H^s is Hilbert via weighted L2
contents.support: The transported first-variable-linear L2 inner product proves the claim.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (2): H^s is included in H^t for s at least t
contents.reason: Order inclusions and their continuous bounds are assigned to FR-6 after this pair establishes each H^s as a space of tempered distributions.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (3): H^0 is L2 and integer norms compare with derivative sums
contents.support: The H^0 equality and exact unitary normalization are included; the integer k>0 comparison is separately deferred in the next row.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (3), integer k>0 derivative-sum norm comparison
contents.reason: The 2pi derivative symbol makes these norms equivalent rather than identical; FR-6 owns the comparison and its constants.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (4): Schwartz inclusion and density in each H^s
contents.support: The density proof is made explicit before transporting completion classes to L2.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (4): every Schwartz function lies in each H^s
contents.support: The B-page calculation uses the bracket multiplier and Schwartz L2 bound.

contents.name: Section 12.1.2 property (5): differentiation lowers Sobolev order
contents.reason: FR-6 is the later multiplier and Sobolev-calculus consumer; derivative mapping is beyond the present completion bridge.

sources.reading: Full PDF downloaded and the specified printed ranges read; the current URL serves a 2026 revision, so locators differ from the 2022 design citation.

sources.title: Richard B. Melrose, Differential Analysis, Chapter 3: Distributions (2017)
sources.locator: Section 4, Fourier inversion and Sobolev spaces, printed pp. 66-70: Proposition 4.3, equations (4.8) and (4.14), Lemma 4.4, Definition 4.5, Proposition 4.6, Propositions 4.7-4.8 and their proofs

contents.name: Proposition 4.3: Fourier transformation is an L2 isomorphism
contents.support: The repository uses the unitary 2pi normalization, unlike the source's unnormalized Fourier integral.

contents.name: Equation (4.8): nonnegative-order Sobolev spaces from weighted Fourier L2
contents.support: The source's Fourier weight motivates the candidate norm; no integer-order comparison is taken from this equation.

contents.name: Lemma 4.4: integer-order derivative characterization
contents.reason: FR-6 separately compares real-order Bessel norms with integer-order weak-derivative Sobolev norms and adjusts the 2pi multiplier constants.

contents.name: Definition 4.5 and Proposition 4.6: Fourier transform on tempered distributions
contents.support: This published interface gives the inverse Fourier transform used by the completion embedding.

contents.name: Equation (4.14): negative and real orders as weighted Fourier distributions
contents.support: The scaffold proves that every such distribution comes from exactly one completion class.

contents.name: Proposition 4.7: negative integer order as derivatives of L2 functions
contents.reason: The pair proves the completion-to-distribution bridge for every real order; an explicit negative-integer derivative decomposition is a separate representation theorem and is not required by the selected consumer.

contents.name: Proposition 4.8: Hilbert structure and Schwartz density in every H^m
contents.support: The Hilbert claim is obtained by a surjective weighted Fourier isometry; its density step is harvested in the next row.

contents.name: Proposition 4.8 proof: Schwartz is dense in the weighted L2 model
contents.support: The local proof spells out the inverse-weight multiplier and inverse Fourier operations.

contents.name: Proposition 4.8: H^m and H^{-m} dual pairing
contents.reason: Duality of positive and negative Sobolev orders is not needed to define the completion, prove its embedding, or characterize its weighted distribution image.

sources.reading: Full chapter PDF downloaded and the complete specified argument range inspected, including the proof of Proposition 4.8; source Fourier normalization is converted to the repository's unitary 2pi convention.

sources.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Linear Analysis and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 3
sources.locator: Chapter 3 opening and Section 3.3, printed pp. 49 and 54-55: notation and assumptions, Definition 3.5 and Theorem 3.6 statement

contents.name: Chapter 3 convention: bounded domain and real-valued weak-derivative Sobolev functions
contents.reason: The current pair uses complex Schwartz and L2 spaces on all of R^n, including negative real orders, so this bounded-domain real convention is not its source interface.

contents.name: Definition 3.5: integer-order weak-derivative W^{k,p} spaces
contents.reason: PDE-11 owns weak-derivative W^{k,p} definitions; this pair defines real-order H^s by completion before FR-6 compares the two.

contents.name: Theorem 3.6: W^{k,p} is Banach and H^k is Hilbert
contents.reason: The theorem concerns integer-order weak derivatives on a domain, which PDE-11 handles; it does not prove the real-order weighted completion claim here.

sources.reading: Full PDF downloaded; the exact named chapter ranges were inspected. This source from the design's source matrix is not counted as direct support for the real-order bridge.
